description: Controlled vocabulary. Every concept in Ekdotico has exactly one canonical term. This file is the single source for the mechanical vocabulary rules: the prose tables in guidelines.md are generated from it, and the linter reads it directly. Adding a term means editing this file and nothing else.

notes.ambiguousVariants: Variants under `ambiguousVariants` are also ordinary English or legitimate domain terms. The linter reports them as substantive and marks them for human confirmation rather than blocking, because a match is necessary but not sufficient. A "faculty dashboard" and an MLA "Works Cited" list are both correct usages.
notes.notDetectable: A term under `notDetectable` is a known non-canonical form that the linter deliberately does not match, because the false-positive rate would drown the signal. Each carries a `notDetectableReason`. These are not exemptions from the rule — reviewers still catch them — only from automation.
notes.scope: A term with `scope: "specification-only"` is canonical in specification, architecture, and engineering contexts but is not a user-facing label. Product copy describes what the writer sees rather than naming the mechanism.

terms.concept: The document the user is working on
terms.rationale: Format-agnostic; applies equally to thesis, journal article, research paper, and conference paper. "Paper" implies a specific physical format. "Manuscript" implies an unpublished state. "Work" is too general for functional contexts. "Manuscript" is also standard academic usage for a paper under submission, so it is confirmable rather than blocking. "Project" names the same thing from the other side: FR-AU uses it for the unit an institution gains read access to — a document together with its source library, planning canvas, research journal, and task list — while every other module calls that unit the document, and the data model has no Project entity. Document is canonical for the concept; FR-AU's wording is a known residue and its amendment is a separate specification change, so "project" is confirmable rather than blocking.

terms.concept: The action of permanently committing the provenance record
terms.rationale: Captures the metaphor of a physical seal on a legal document — closure, integrity, authenticity — without requiring users to understand the technical mechanism. "Lock" implies reversibility. "Finalise" is too generic. Sealing is what the writer does; export lock is the mechanism that carries it out, and the two are separate entries rather than synonyms.

terms.concept: The mechanism that seals the provenance record at export
terms.rationale: The established name in the specification, where it is used throughout FR-EX, FR-PR, and FR-VR. It names a mechanism, not an action the writer takes: the writer exports, and the export lock is what seals the record as part of that. Distinct from Seal, which is the user-facing action.
terms.scopeNote: Correct and canonical in specification, architecture, and engineering contexts. Not a user-facing label. The writer encounters the mechanism as part of Export and is informed that the provenance record is sealed at that point; product copy says the document is sealed on export rather than naming the mechanism. Recording the scope resolves a contradiction carried since 0.2, where the controlled vocabulary called the term non-user-facing while the specification used it as the primary name — the term was never wrong, only its scope was unstated. The short form "lock" and the participle "locked" are correct within the same specification context, which is why they are no longer carried as variants of Seal.

terms.concept: The state of a document after sealing
terms.rationale: Past participle and adjective form of the canonical verb.

terms.concept: The complete collection of captured provenance data
terms.rationale: The record is the complete, structured collection of all data the provenance system captures for a document; its human-readable rendering is the provenance report. Established throughout the SRS. "Record" alone is too generic in other contexts. "Certificate" implies third-party issuance. "Writing record" omits the integrity dimension.

terms.concept: The human-readable rendering of the provenance record
terms.rationale: The report is the legible presentation of the provenance record, returned on verify.ekdoti.co and in the faculty dashboard. The record is the data; the report is the view of it. A report is always a rendering of a record, never a separate artefact.

terms.concept: The AI-assisted prose editing tool
terms.rationale: Locked. Title case; two words. Never "humanize" or "humanise".

terms.concept: The mind map and planning feature
terms.rationale: Specific to Ekdotico; distinguishes from the generic "mind map" methodology and from the LMS named Canvas. Communicates the purpose. "Canvas" alone is acceptable shorthand after "planning canvas" has appeared once in the same document or screen — the LMS ambiguity is resolved by first use rather than by avoiding the short form throughout.

terms.concept: A continuous unit of writing activity
terms.rationale: Shortest, most functional term. A session begins when an authenticated user opens or activates a document and performs a qualifying interaction; opening or activating a document without one begins nothing, and no provenance data is recorded for activity consisting solely of non-qualifying events. It ends when the document tab is closed or navigated away from, when the collaboration connection is lost and is not re-established within the grace period, or after a continuous absence of qualifying interactions exceeding the inactivity threshold. The grace period and the threshold are specified in the SRS (FR-PR-02, FR-PR-03), which governs; naming the values here would put two documents in a position to disagree about them. "Writing session" is acceptable in instructional prose on first use; "session" is the canonical term for functional and provenance contexts.

terms.concept: A main-line document version created from an existing sealed document
terms.rationale: Established in the branching specification.

terms.concept: The action of creating a main-line revision
terms.rationale: Established in the branching specification. Available on main-line (.0) documents only.

terms.concept: A derived document based on a sealed document
terms.rationale: Established in the branching specification. Noun and verb. "Fork" is also the ordinary software sense — a forked dependency, or forking the open-source repository — so it is confirmable rather than blocking.
terms.notDetectableReason: "Copy" is the house term for prose itself — the Expression Guidelines use it on almost every line — so matching it produces noise on a scale that would train reviewers to ignore the linter. A rule that cries wolf on the system's own core noun is worse than no rule. Reviewers catch a document called a copy; the linter does not try.

terms.concept: The two-component version identifier
terms.rationale: Always followed by major.minor format, for example Version 1.0. Established in the branching specification. Always two-component.

terms.concept: The SHA-256 hash identifying a sealed export
terms.rationale: Technical term; displayed in monospace. Not user-facing in plain prose.

terms.concept: The Ed25519 signature appended at the end of each session
terms.rationale: Distinguishes the per-session signing event from the export-level hash.

terms.concept: The AI-powered search and source discovery surface
terms.rationale: Established in SRS module naming.

terms.concept: The AI query-assistance surface inside the research workspace
terms.rationale: The fifth AI surface, and the last one to be named. It carried three labels — "research workspace assistant" in FR-AU-40, "AI-powered query assistance" in FR-RW-22, and "research assistant" on the deferred-registers page — while the vocabulary held no entry for it at all, which is how a concept ends up with one name per module. FR-AU-40 enumerates the five surfaces an institutional AI policy governs, so its label is the one the policy screen will carry and the one adopted here. The surface reads the document and suggests search queries; it does not conduct the search, which the research workspace does, and the two are separate entries rather than one. "Research assistant" is a person in an academic setting and is confirmable rather than blocking; "query assistance" remains correct as a description of what the surface does, and is a breach only when used as its name.

terms.concept: The PDF reading and annotation surface
terms.rationale: Simple and functional. "PDF annotator" is secondary. The compound module title "PDF reader and annotator" is permitted where it names the FR-PD module rather than the product surface. "PDF viewer" also means a third-party application reading an exported file — the metadata entry visible in Acrobat's properties panel, for instance — so it is confirmable rather than blocking.

terms.concept: The AI-powered source interaction surface
terms.rationale: Established in SRS module naming.

terms.concept: The AI-maintained writing journal
terms.rationale: Established in SRS module naming.

terms.concept: The task management surface
terms.rationale: Established in SRS module naming. "Task panel" names the panel within the tracker rather than the tracker itself, and the specification uses it that way throughout FR-TK.

terms.concept: The highest-confidence tier in task extraction, which creates a task without a confirmation step
terms.rationale: The tier was called auto-complete while the task it creates is assigned status "open", so the name described the opposite of the behaviour and four pages disagreed about what the tier does. Renamed by the September 2026 documentation audit: the tier is named for what it does, which is add the task. "Auto-complete" is confirmable rather than blocking because it is also correct English for a different mechanism in the same module — FR-TK-10 reassesses existing tasks and genuinely marks them complete, and "auto-completed tasks" there is right. The tier name and the completion action are two concepts that happen to share a word; only the first is this entry.

terms.concept: The citation resolution subsystem
terms.rationale: Resolves academic identifiers — DOIs, arXiv IDs, PMIDs, ISBNs — against external bibliographic sources and returns structured metadata. Consistent with the FR-CI module. "Auto-" was dropped in 0.3: the engine does not generate citations, it retrieves and validates them, and the prefix implied an automation the subsystem does not perform. Three forms were in circulation before the term was locked.

terms.concept: The bibliography display and management surface
terms.rationale: Established in SRS module naming. "Reference manager" is also the product category occupied by Zotero and Mendeley; naming a competitor category is not a vocabulary breach.

terms.concept: An individual reference entry in the bibliography
terms.rationale: Standard academic term; consistent with the FR-CI module.

terms.concept: The formatted list of all citations
terms.rationale: Standard academic term. Note that "Works Cited" and "Reference list" remain correct when naming the style-specific output of MLA and APA respectively.

terms.concept: An inline block of typeset mathematical content
terms.rationale: Consistent with the FR-LX module. "Equation block" is also a document structure term, used when describing exported output and numbering rather than the editor feature.

terms.concept: An inline block diagram
terms.rationale: Consistent with the FR-MD module.

terms.concept: The public endpoint for record verification
terms.rationale: Always lowercase; no "the" or "portal" prefix. "The verifier" was removed as a variant: it names the person performing verification, not the endpoint.

terms.concept: The free individual plan
terms.rationale: Established in the SRS and product documentation. "Free tier" is also the general term for competitor pricing, which the market analysis has to use.

terms.concept: The paid individual plan
terms.rationale: Established in the SRS and product documentation.

terms.concept: The institutional plan with supervisor access
terms.rationale: Established in the SRS and product documentation.

terms.concept: A user on the Team Plan with supervisor access rights
terms.rationale: Used in the SRS. Not "faculty" (too specific to one context) and not "reviewer" (too generic). "Advisor" is not a synonym here: in Ekdotico it names the Prose Refine writing advisor. "Faculty dashboard" is the established surface name and is unaffected. "Reviewer" is also one of the four document permission roles in FR-ED and is used generically for a person reading a record, so it is confirmable rather than blocking. "Instructor" is also used generically when enumerating who might verify a record, so it is confirmable rather than blocking.

terms.concept: Edits not yet saved to the server
terms.rationale: Standard UI term; unambiguous. "Pending changes" also describes queued synchronisation state in the planning canvas, which is a different concept from the unsaved-changes indicator.

terms.concept: The action of producing a file from the document
terms.rationale: Standard term. Verb and noun.

terms.concept: Creating a new document
terms.rationale: Functional label; matches the action button label.

gaps.description: Concepts that recur in Ekdotico content but have no canonical term yet. Recorded here so the linter does not flag them and so the additions process has a queue. These are gaps in the guidelines, not failures of the content. Surfaced by the Phase 1 audit, 2026-08-09.

concepts.concept: The unit of collaborative content in the editor
The per-document collection of saved sources
The institutional container for documents and policy
The three confidence bands in task extraction
The person writing, in prose contexts
concepts.note: Escalate. Five synonyms for the primary user is the reliability-contract failure principle P7 exists to prevent, and it compounds with every page added.
